title: Synthesis of CFET Cell Library Leveraging Backside Metal Routing
problem: Complementary FET (CFET) technology stacks PMOS and NMOS vertically, reducing routing tracks and increasing routing complexity; current synthesis lacks backside metal (BS) routing utilization and transistor folding efficiency.
method: The work introduces backside metal routing utilization at cell synthesis stage and efficient transistor folding handling. Euler path analysis estimates lower bounds on contacted poly pitch (CPP); dynamic programming calculates frontside minimum required tracks (FMRT); satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) determines final device placement and routing.

title: Location is Key: Leveraging LLM for Functional Bug Localization in Verilog Design
problem: Automatic Verilog bug localization methods only suggest buggy line sets rather than precise identification, and depend on expert-written verification tools.
method: LiK is a specialized Verilog LLM trained from Deepseek-Coder via continuous pre-training, supervised fine-tuning on bug localization, and reinforcement learning to reduce localization errors.

title: SNAcc: An Open-Source Framework for Streaming-based Network-to-Storage Accelerators
problem: General purpose CPUs struggle to keep up with current Ethernet line speeds in network-to-storage pipelines, wasting compute resources and bandwidth for storage management.
method: Open-source framework leveraging FPGA flexible communication interfaces (Ethernet and PCIe) for direct NVMe access without host CPU interaction; DNN-based classification case study on image streams.

title: Enabling Ahead Prediction with Practical Energy Constraints
problem: Branch predictors require multiple pipeline cycles to produce a prediction, causing a latency penalty; ahead prediction solves this by starting early but must consider all 2^N possible histories for the N intermediate branches, increasing energy by 14.6x and making the approach impractical.
method: The authors observe that most of the 2^N possible intermediate branch-direction combinations never actually occur at runtime; only one or two patterns are observed in practice. They modify the TAGE predictor to track and eliminate non-materializing history patterns, reducing the number of parallel prediction paths that must be evaluated. This allows the ahead predictor to operate with only 1.5x energy overhead instead of the previously assumed 14.6x, while delivering 4.4% IPC improvement.

title: LAMMPS-KOKKOS: Performance Portable Molecular Dynamics Across Exascale Architectures
problem: LAMMPS molecular dynamics code must adapt to modern heterogeneous computing with multi-vendor GPUs while maintaining performance portability
method: Integration of Kokkos performance portability library into LAMMPS C++ codebase; implementation and optimization for pairwise, many-body reactive, and ML-based potentials

title: Optimizing Data Acquisitions in Multi-Robot Systems
problem: Multi-robot systems lack efficient mechanisms for real-time cross-robot data acquisition; traditional file systems fail to exploit robot data temporal locality
method: ROSfs user-level filesystem: labeled sub-file organization with time-indexed queries for active data; integrates with ROS ecosystem; evaluated on physical UAV/UGV platforms

title: Dynamic Load Balancer in Intel Xeon Scalable Processor: Performance Analyses, Enhancements, and Guidelines
problem: Rapid growth in inter-host networking speed causes bursty, unevenly distributed traffic across CPU cores, leading to excessive queuing delays and service latency variance; hardware-based load balancing with the Intel DLB still consumes significant host CPU cycles to prepare and enqueue work descriptors for received packets.
method: The paper first benchmarks DLB against software load balancers with a microbenchmark suite. It then proposes AccDirect, a system architecture and software co-design that exploits PCIe Peer-to-Peer (P2P) communication to create a direct path between the NIC and DLB, eliminating the host CPU from the descriptor enqueue path. The NIC directly enqueues work descriptors to DLB hardware queues using P2P DMA, removing all CPU cycles from the load-balancing hot path.

title: A Differential Series-Resonance CMOS VCO with Pole-Convergence Technique Achieving 202.1 dBc/Hz FoMTA at 10MHz Offset
problem: Achieving ultra-low phase noise in voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs) for high-speed wireless/wireline communications and high-speed ADC/DACs is challenging; multicore VCOs achieve low phase noise but suffer from area, mismatch, and design complexity, while series-resonance VCOs have not yet been demonstrated in pure CMOS technology.
method: A differential series-resonance CMOS VCO implements a novel pole-convergence technique to achieve ultra-low phase noise. The design exploits series-resonance topology (SR-VCO) to avoid area and mismatch penalties of multicore approaches, using differential architecture to improve noise performance while maintaining pure CMOS compatibility.

title: Lightweight CNN-Based Artifact Reduction for Scientific Error-bounded Lossy Compression
problem: Lossy compression widely used for large-scale scientific data but introduces artifacts that compromise analysis. Error-bounded compressors (SZ, ZFP) provide tight control but artifacts remain visible. Need post-processing method to improve reconstruction quality without excessive overhead.
method: Lightweight 3D CNN architecture with fixed-scale batch normalization for stable training and fast inference. Empirically analyze network size vs. minimum achievable MSE loss. Validate generalizability across compressors (SZ1, SZ2, SZP, SZX, ZFP) and scientific domains.

title: A Compact Full-Duplex Receiver with Wideband Multi-Domain Hilbert-Transform-Equalization Cancellation Based on Multi-Stage APFs Achieving 65dB SIC Across 120MHz BW
problem: Full-duplex (FD) receiver self-interference cancellation (SIC) techniques face a tradeoff between delay-bandwidth product (DBW), noise figure, and power consumption; most existing cancellers achieve <80MHz cancellation bandwidth with >30dB depth, while frequency-domain equalization-based approaches require power-hungry high-Q filters with noise degradation.
method: The FD receiver employs multi-domain Hilbert-transform-equalization (HTE) SIC with cascaded low-noise allpass filters (APFs): 1st-order APF in RF canceller tap for flat frequency response, 2nd-order APF with delay-peaking in 2nd tap for extended DBW, achieving 65dB SIC over 120MHz with <10% RF delay variation.

title: Generative Latent Diffusion for Efficient Spatiotemporal Data Reduction
problem: Generative models offer compression but lack controllability and reconstruction accuracy for practical data compression; existing compressors (SZ3) have limited compression ratios
method: Latent diffusion combining VAE with conditional diffusion model; compresses keyframes into latent space for interpolation of remaining frames; eliminates per-frame latent storage

title: 13.3 A Cryo-BiCMOS Controller for 9Be+-Trapped-Ion-Based Quantum Computers
problem: Trapped-ion quantum computers require cryogenic control electronics operating at ~4K to interface with ion traps; existing digital controllers consume excessive power and limit qubit scalability.
method: Cryo-BiCMOS (bipolar + CMOS) controller operating at 4K for trapped-ion systems; leverages bipolar transistors' superior low-temperature performance and CMOS for integration. Implements quantum-charge-coupled-device (QCCD) control for ion shuttling and entanglement operations.

title: Ensembler: Protect Collaborative Inference Privacy from Model Inversion Attack via Selective Ensemble
problem: Collaborative inference allows cloud providers to reconstruct sensitive client inputs via model inversion attacks; existing defenses either sacrifice privacy or add prohibitive overhead.
method: Uses selective ensemble on server-side: multiple model branches ensemble predictions to obfuscate gradient signals, making input reconstruction harder while maintaining inference accuracy with <5% overhead.

title: PARO: Hardware-Software Co-design with Pattern-aware Reorder-based Attention Quantization in Video Generation Models
problem: 3D full attention in video generation models creates massive attention maps (56.50 GB for CogVideoX-5B) consuming excessive computation time (1 min per 49-frame video on A100).
method: PARO investigates diverse 3D full attention patterns and proposes reorder technique unifying them into block-diagonal structure. Block-wise mixed-precision quantization achieves lossless compression at 4.80-bit average. Output-bitwidth aware PE array co-design optimizes mixed-precision QK multiplication.

title: 22.3 A 42Gb/s Single-Ended Hybrid-DFE PAM-3 Receiver for GDDR7 Memory Interfaces
problem: GDDR7 PAM3 receivers must achieve 42Gb/s while managing inter-symbol interference (ISI) and tight feedback timing constraints in direct-feedback (DF) DFE implementations.
method: A hybrid DFE combining direct-feedback and loop-unrolled (LU) techniques reduces feedback time constraints while minimizing area and power overhead, enabling 42Gb/s PAM3 reception.

title: Pipirima: Predicting Patterns in Sparsity to Accelerate Matrix Algebra
problem: Sparse accelerators struggle with load imbalance when processing compressed sparse matrices due to unpredictable non-zero value distributions, limiting performance despite sparsity optimization opportunities.
method: Pipirima predicts non-zero value patterns in sparse matrices using resource-friendly simple counters inspired by branch predictors. During streaming of CSR-compressed matrices, predictor anticipates non-zero locations to enable proactive acceleration. Evaluated on SpMV and SpMM kernels.
